clues.text: Urged to leave her mother-in-law Naomi, she replied, "Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God."
Gleaning grain behind the harvesters near Bethlehem, she happened to come to the part of the field owned by Boaz.
After Boaz ate and drank and lay down by the grain heap, she went in secretly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.
Matthew's list of Jesus' ancestors names her as the mother of Obed, the father of Jesse.
The women of Bethlehem told Naomi this daughter-in-law loved her and was better to her than seven sons.
Bowing face down in a Bethlehem field, she asked Boaz why he took notice of her, since she was a foreigner.
Before witnesses, Boaz declared he had acquired Mahlon's widow as his wife to raise up the dead man's name.
